newsitem.title: RUSSIA: TABLE - Russian payments deficit narrows in 1st qtr.
newsitem.headline: TABLE - Russian payments deficit narrows in 1st qtr.

text.p: Russia's overall balance of payments deficit, reflecting the net losses of its financial and trade transactions with the rest of the world, narrowed to $1.94 billion in the first quarter of this year, according to official figures.
The capital account deficit, representing net investment and debt outflows, narrowed sharply to $2.11 billion, the Russian European Centre for Economic Policy (RECEP) said, quoting central bank data.
The central bank said the current account surplus, the balance of trade and services, widened to $4.86 billion.
Russia was able to increase net reserves by $1.33 billion in the first quarter.
But it borrowed $646 million from the International Monetary Fund and $168 million from other international financial institutions to fund the first quarter deficit, RECEP said.
Russia also rescheduled $1.32 billion and deferred $881 million of former borrowings, so that debt service was only $1.4 billion in the first quarter.

The central bank and RECEP, itself quoting central bank data, issued the following figures in millions of dollars, for transactions with all countries, including Baltic states and members of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
Use of IMF credits and loans 646 672 1,393
NOTES - *IFIs -- international financial institutions. Differences due to rounding.
Other investment assets (minus sign indicates build-up of item or capital export, positive figure indicates reduction of item or capital repatriation)
Hard currency cash -- purchases of dollars by Russian households who typically hold savings in cash at home. Figure -2,675 shows households bought $2.675 billion of cash dollars.
Bank accounts and deposits -- additional savings placed in foreign-currency accounts, mainly by households.
Trade credits -- credits mainly to countries still relying on cheap supplies of Russian natural resources.

Overdue payments -- shows payments not made on Russian exports and credits, including non-payment for Russian energy by former Soviet republics and other East European countries. The figure of 1,268 shows a reduction in these assets as some overdue payments are received.
Non-repatriated export revenue -- the figure of -716 reflects profits of natural resource exporters legally removed from export receipts and kept in foreign currency.
Loans received -- figure of -2,433 shows loans received and unpaid debts falling due during the year.
Errors and omissions -- could reflect illegal capital flight.
